DEVIATION REPORT
Cross-Border Data Transfer Agreement — Counterparty Markup Reconciliation
Data Privacy / Cybersecurity Practice
Matter File 9 — "Analyze Counterparty Markup of Cross-Border Data Transfer Agreement — Deviation Report"

---------------------------------------------------------------------
I. SCOPE AND PURPOSE

This deviation report reconciles the counterparty's latest markup of the Cross-Border Data Transfer Agreement against our original draft and the firm-standard playbook, incorporating (i) the transfer impact summary for the cross-border flows and (ii) the controlling partner instructions reflected in the deal team correspondence.

The counterparty's revision accepts most firm-standard provisions but introduces three (3) material deviations that must be identified and reconciled against the base materials, the applicable data privacy and cybersecurity framework, and the disclosure schedules. As directed, all scheduled exceptions (which control over general statements in the base materials) have been reconciled against the markup's changes.

---------------------------------------------------------------------
II. DOCUMENTS RELIED UPON

1. Base materials / Original draft (Deal materials, Matter File 9): operative Cross-Border Data Transfer Agreement containing representations and warranties, covenants, conditions to closing, indemnification, and termination provisions.
2. Counterparty markup (the revision under review).
3. Schedules and Exhibits to the agreement (Schedule 3.7 — pending regulatory inquiries; Schedule 5.2 — retained liabilities; Exhibit B — survival matrix). These scheduled exceptions control.
4. Deal team correspondence (partner instructions) — the LATEST message controls and supersedes any contrary earlier message.
5. Transfer impact summary for the cross-border personal data flows (regulatory framework analysis).

Note: an unrelated administrative correspondence file was misfiled into this matter folder. It concerns a different engagement and has been excluded from this analysis.

---------------------------------------------------------------------
III. PARTNER INSTRUCTIONS (CONTROLLING)

The latest controlling instruction establishes the following analysis priorities:

• The client WILL CONCEDE the counterparty's basket conversion (converting the deductible to a tipping basket). This concession is acceptable and should not be treated as a contested point.

• Any reduction of the survival period for the core representations is a WALK-AWAY ISSUE and must be rejected as a non-negotiable point.

Earlier messages that stated the opposite priority ordering are superseded and do not govern.

---------------------------------------------------------------------
IV. DEVIATION-BY-DEVIATION ANALYSIS

DEVIATION 1 — Indemnification Cap Reduced and Basket Converted from a Deductible to a Tipping Basket

Counterparty markup action:
• The indemnification cap is silently reduced relative to our original draft.
• The basket is converted from a deductible (dollar-for-dollar recovery above the threshold) to a tipping basket (first-dollar recovery only once the threshold is exceeded).

Reconciliation against base materials and schedules:
• Schedule 5.2 lists retained liabilities that the indemnification changes would silently shift. The reduction in the cap, combined with the basket mechanics change, alters the economic allocation of those retained liabilities to the detriment of the client absent a corresponding pricing or scope adjustment.
• Under the controlling partner instruction, the basket conversion is CONCEDED. Accordingly, we take no issue with the conversion of the deductible to a tipping basket.
• The cap reduction, however, is separate and distinct from the conceded basket conversion. The silent reduction of the indemnification cap is NOT covered by the concession and remains a contested deviation. Recommend rejecting the cap reduction or seeking an increase to preserve the economic protection reflected in the base materials, particularly given the retained liabilities in Schedule 5.2.

Position: CONCEDE the basket conversion (per partner instruction); REJECT/CONTEST the silent reduction of the indemnification cap.

---------------------------------------------------------------------

DEVIATION 2 — Material Adverse Effect (MAE) Definition Adds Carve-Outs for Regulatory Action

Counterparty markup action:
• The definition of Material Adverse Effect is expanded with carve-outs for regulatory action "of exactly the kind at issue in this matter."

Reconciliation against base materials and schedules:
• Schedule 3.7 discloses two (2) pending regulatory inquiries. The markup's new MAE carve-outs are calibrated to exclude precisely these regulatory actions from what would otherwise constitute a Material Adverse Effect.
• The disclosure schedules must be reconciled against the expansion. Because Schedule 3.7 already puts the client on notice of the two pending inquiries, the carve-outs would allow the counterparty to disclaim liability for a regulatory development arising from matters the counterparty already knew were in scope.
• In a cross-border data transfer context, this intersects the transfer impact summary: the regulatory exposure arising from the international data flows (data protection authority scrutiny, adequacy determinations, or enforcement on the transferred data) is precisely the kind of regulatory action this carve-out would shield.
• The scheduled exception (Schedule 3.7) controls over the general MAE statement. The carve-outs unreasonably narrow a core closing condition and are not supported by the base materials.

Position: REJECT the MAE carve-outs absent a narrowing that excludes only genuinely unforeseen regulatory action and preserves the client's protection for the two disclosed pending inquiries and associated cross-border data-protection exposure.

---------------------------------------------------------------------

DEVIATION 3 — New Limitation Period Shortens Survival for the Core Representations

Counterparty markup action:
• A new limitation period shortens the survival window for the core representations.

Reconciliation against base materials and schedules:
• Exhibit B sets the survival matrix for the core representations. The markup's shortened limitation period directly contradicts the survival matrix in Exhibit B.
• Survival of the core representations is a threshold structural protection; truncating the survival period reduces the period during which the client may pursue a claim for a breach of a core representation.
• Under the controlling partner instruction, any survival-period reduction is a WALK-AWAY ISSUE and must be rejected as non-negotiable.

Position: REJECT the limitation-period reduction. This is a walk-away issue per the controlling partner instruction; do not concede, and treat failure to restore the Exhibit B survival matrix as grounds to walk away from the transaction.

---------------------------------------------------------------------
V. TRANSFER IMPACT SUMMARY — APPLICATION

The transfer impact assessment for the cross-border personal data flows informs the analysis as follows:

• Regulatory action arising from the international data transfer (DPA investigation, adequacy/challenge, or enforcement relating to the transferred data) is the gateway risk that the counterparty's MAE carve-outs (Deviation 2) seek to carve out. Because the transfer impact summary identifies this regulatory exposure as live and material, the carve-outs must not be permitted to shield it.
• The retained liabilities shifted by the indemnification changes (Deviation 1) include data-protection related exposure. The cap reduction would operate to cap recovery for those transfer-related liabilities, which the transfer impact summary flags as a principal exposure.
• The survival-period reduction (Deviation 3) would cut off claims on the core data-privacy representations within an unreasonably short window, undermining the ongoing compliance and enforcement exposure reflected in the transfer impact summary.

The deviation report therefore treats the transfer impact summary as a live integrating consideration: the deviations disproportionately erode protection on precisely the cross-border data-privacy exposure the summary identifies as principal.

---------------------------------------------------------------------
VI. RECOMMENDED POSITIONS SUMMARY

| Deviation | Counterparty Action | Recommended Position |
|-----------|--------------------|----------------------|
| 1a | Indemnification cap silently reduced | REJECT / contest the cap reduction |
| 1b | Basket converted deductible → tipping | CONCEDE (per partner instruction) |
| 2 | MAE adds carve-outs for regulatory action | REJECT absent narrowing; do not carve out disclosed/pending regulatory exposure |
| 3 | Limitation period shortens core rep survival | REJECT — walk-away issue; restore Exhibit B survival matrix |

---------------------------------------------------------------------
VII. WALK-AWAY / NON-NEGOTIABLE POINTS

Pursuant to the controlling partner instructions, the following is a non-negotiable, walk-away point:

• Any reduction of the survival period for the core representations (Deviation 3) — the agreement must retain the Exhibit B survival matrix in full.

---------------------------------------------------------------------
VIII. CONCESSIONS

The following is an acceptable concession per the controlling partner instructions:

• Conversion of the indemnity basket from a deductible to a tipping basket (Deviation 1b).

---------------------------------------------------------------------
IX. CONCLUSION

The counterparty's markup introduces three deviation types. Two (the indemnification cap reduction and the shortened survival period) materially undermine the client's protection and are not covered by the limited concession. One (the basket conversion) is an acceptable concession directed by the partner. The MAE carve-outs must be rejected because, reconciled against Schedule 3.7 and the transfer impact summary, they shield exactly the regulatory and cross-border data exposure at issue. The deliverable reflects the controlling partner instruction: concede the basket, hold firm on the survival matrix as a walk-away point, and resist the cap reduction and the MAE carve-outs.
